world.h: Iran war: Saudi coalition hits Houthi sites
world.b: Al Jazeera live updates: the Saudi-led coalition hits key Houthi sites, and an Aramco building is struck in Dhahran.
world.title: Saudi coalition hits key Houthi sites; Aramco building struck in Dhahran

world.h: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer
world.b: The Vatican said Pope Leo XIV was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma after surgery to remove the lower lobe of his right lung. It gave no details on treatment or outlook.

world.h: UN sees 'window' for peace in eastern DR Congo
world.b: UN Great Lakes envoy Huang Xia told the Security Council that US- and Qatar-led peace processes have made 'notable progress' in eastern DR Congo.
world.title: UN official says ‘window of opportunity’ for peace in DR Congo

world.h: Iran war: Houthi missiles hit Aramco building
world.b: Al Jazeera live updates: the Houthis fire a missile barrage at Saudi Arabia, and an Aramco building is hit.

world.h: Cholera cases triple in Yemen, WHO warns
world.b: Suspected cholera cases in Yemen tripled in three weeks, from 217 to 647 a week, as fighting drove more than 200,000 people into unsanitary camps, the WHO said.
world.title: Cholera cases surge in Yemen as conflict intensifies, WHO says

world.h: MI5 chief: Iran targeting UK military bases
world.b: MI5 Director-General Ken McCallum said Iran is stepping up attempts to strike harder targets like military sites in Britain. Tehran denies involvement.

world.h: Houthis threaten Saudi Aramco sites and airports
world.b: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree called Saudi Aramco facilities and airports 'a legitimate target' after the Saudi-led coalition ordered civilians to evacuate an oil station in Sanaa.

world.h: Ex-DR Congo leader Kabila joins M23 in coalition
world.b: Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila launched a new political and military coalition that includes the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, which has captured vast areas of eastern DR Congo.

world.h: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria's coast
world.b: Two ships were hit in drone attacks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one sank, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. One was the Ukrainian-owned, Maltese-flagged Chelsea 3.

world.h: Trump hedges on Netanyahu as Israel vote nears
world.b: Despite years of policies that buoyed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, President Trump is hedging ahead of Israel's election.

national.h: CVS to pay $315M to settle opioid case
national.b: CVS agreed to pay $315 million to settle a 2024 Justice Department lawsuit over medically unnecessary opioid prescriptions.
national.title: CVS agrees to pay $315 million to settle Justice Department case over opioid prescriptions

national.h: Florida carries out 17th execution of the year
national.b: Florida executed a prisoner who killed his cellmate in hopes of getting a death sentence.
national.title: Florida executed a prisoner who killed his cellmate in hopes of getting a death sentence. It's the state's 17th execution of the year

national.b: Cornell suspended all Interfraternity Council parties through the 2026-27 year and gave State Police a role in investigating campus sex crimes, amid outrage over a 2024 assault case.

national.h: Scammers drain SNAP cards; Congress won't fund fix
national.b: ProPublica: organized gangs are stealing SNAP benefits with card skimmers. Most theft could be blocked by chip cards, but Congress won't fund the switch.
national.title: Scammers Are Stealing Millions From Food Stamp Recipients. Congress Could Fix It — but Won’t.

national.h: Pennsylvania inmates wait years on lawyers
national.b: ProPublica: underfunded, flat-fee post-conviction lawyers in Pennsylvania fell months or years behind, some leaving clients waiting as long as a decade.
national.title: He Waited Nine Years in Prison for His Lawyer to File a Single Brief. In This State, There’s No Rule Against It.

politics.h: Judge blocks White House press ban for now
politics.b: A federal judge ruled Trump cannot bar more than 70 journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House over their coverage, at least until a trial.
politics.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico prevail against White House — for now

politics.h: Poll: Most say Trump puts his wealth first
politics.b: An AP-NORC poll found over half of US adults say Trump's second term serves his own business interests 'a lot'; only 11% say he represents regular Americans.

politics.h: Guilfoyle resigns as ambassador to Greece
politics.b: Kimberly Guilfoyle resigned amid misconduct allegations, including claims she offered a donor access to officials for money. The White House said it had asked her to resign.

politics.h: Supreme Court sides with Trump on DOGE records
politics.b: The Supreme Court intervened for a second time in CREW's lawsuit seeking records from Elon Musk's Department of Government Efficiency, siding with the administration.

international.h: China, North Korea to open Yalu River bridge
international.b: The New Yalu River Bridge opens to traffic Thursday, Xinhua reports. China finished its side in 2014, but North Korea left its side unfinished for years.
international.title: China and North Korea to open New Yalu River Bridge, state media reports

international.h: West Bank Palestinians have no say in Israel vote
international.b: Nearly three million Palestinians in the occupied West Bank cannot vote in Israel's Oct. 27 election, unlike 700,000 Jewish settlers living there.
international.title: ‘Like we don’t exist’: Palestinians in West Bank denied say in Israel vote

international.h: Nord Stream sabotage trial opens in Germany
international.b: A Ukrainian former military officer went on trial in Hamburg, accused of organising the 2022 blasts on the Nord Stream gas pipelines. The trial is expected to run into February.
international.title: Ukrainian ex-officer goes on trial in Germany over Nord Stream blasts

international.h: Israel returns 22 stolen artefacts to Greece
international.b: Israel returned 22 ancient artefacts stolen from Greece. Officials gave no details on how they were found.

international.h: Jamaica takes first third-country US deportees
international.b: Twenty-two deportees from the US arrived in Kingston on Tuesday, Jamaica's first third-country deportations under expanding Trump administration agreements.
Colombia's transitional justice tribunal charged 10 former FARC members with war crimes and crimes against humanity against Indigenous people between 1996 and 2016.
international.title: Colombia peace tribunal charges ex-FARC members with anti-Indigenous crimes

international.h: Israeli strike kills one in Gaza City
international.b: An Israeli air strike on a vehicle in Gaza City's Tuffah neighbourhood killed one person, and journalists were wounded in the occupied West Bank.
Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam announced an overnight curfew in parts of Mauritius after a police officer's shooting of a woman sparked unrest.
Riot police in Tirana fired tear gas and water cannons at student protesters who hurled bricks at the Education Ministry and demanded PM Edi Rama resign.

international.h: Russia arrests Japanese reporter as spy
international.b: The FSB arrested Japanese journalist Imai Yuki on Sakhalin Island, accusing him of gathering defence information for Japanese intelligence. The charge carries up to 20 years.

international.h: China sentences 3 to death over Myanmar scams
international.b: A court in Fujian province sentenced three members of the 'Wei family criminal gang' to death for running scam centres in Myanmar.
Yemen's internationally recognised government said it carried out nine air strikes on Houthi positions in Taiz governorate on Tuesday.

international.h: Sweden's Andersson fails again to form government
international.b: Social Democrat leader Magdalena Andersson said talks with the left-wing bloc hit an impasse, prolonging deadlock a month after elections.

international.h: Israeli forces raid Palestinian NGOs in West Bank
international.b: Israeli forces raided the offices of the Union of Palestinian Women's Committees and the Addameer prisoner rights group, and the courtyard of the Palestine Medical Complex.
Delhi police detained leaders of the youth-led 'cockroach' movement after they jumped barricades at a protest site, demanding the chief election commissioner resign over voter list revisions.

international.h: Imran Khan's PTI to fight Khyber takeover
international.b: Jailed ex-PM Imran Khan's party is preparing to fight Pakistan's emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which suspended the PTI-led provincial government.

international.h: Cyberattack spoils food at French supermarkets
international.b: A cyberattack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of French supermarkets pushed fridge temperatures as high as 50C (122F), spoiling food and causing fires. Intermarche, Cooperative U and E Leclerc confirmed the attack.

international.h: 100+ foreign trekkers stranded by Nepal floods
international.b: More than 100 foreign trekkers are stranded in Nepal's Gorkha district after flash floods washed away bridges, hiking trails and hundreds of homes, a local official said.

business.h: Singapore economy grows 5.4% on AI boom
business.b: Singapore's GDP grew 5.4% year-on-year in the third quarter, down from 6.2% in the second, advance estimates showed.
business.title: Singapore’s economy grows more than 5 percent amid AI boom

business.h: Bank of America fined $1.2B by Treasury
business.b: The US Treasury imposed more than $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America for anti-money laundering and sanctions violations.

business.h: Big banks open earnings season mixed
business.b: JPMorgan Chase missed expectations as JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs and Citigroup reported. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley report Wednesday.
business.title: "Can't go to the moon every quarter": Big banks' bumpy start to earning season

business.h: UnitedHealth profits rise as revenue falls
business.b: UnitedHealth's third-quarter revenue declined after losing Medicaid and employer plan members, but its profits went up.
business.title: UnitedHealth stopped insuring some people. Its profits rose.

business.b: The Social Security Administration announces next year's cost-of-living adjustment Wednesday morning. AARP predicts a 3.6% increase for 2027.
business.title: Social Security payments to increase — slightly

science.b: NASA said its JPL-built Perseverance Mars rover broke the record for the longest distance traveled by a vehicle on another planet on Oct. 11.

science.h: Eastern Pacific sets hurricane energy record
science.b: The eastern Pacific passed its 2018 record for accumulated cyclone energy on Sunday, with Hurricane Simon still going strong.

science.h: Seabirds help keep coral reefs healthy
science.b: At Palmyra Atoll in the Pacific, scientists have found a surprising link between seabirds and the health of surrounding coral reefs.

science.h: Anthropic: small AI may soon self-replicate
science.b: Anthropic researchers said in a report Monday that small AI models may be months away from being able to self-replicate on consumer devices such as smart TVs and fridges, without a data centre.

sports.h: Rams cut kicker Mevis after loss to Bills
sports.b: The Rams are releasing Harrison Mevis, who missed two field goals including a 48-yard overtime try, and signing Blake Grupe off the Jets' practice squad.

sports.h: Dream, Valkyries set for WNBA Finals
sports.b: Atlanta and Golden State, neither of which has won a WNBA title, meet in the Finals starting Oct. 17. The Dream are 5-0 in the playoffs.
sports.title: 2026 WNBA playoffs bracket: WNBA Finals schedule tweaked so Dream can use larger venue

sports.b: CBS Sports' annual ranking of the NBA's top 100 players puts Victor Wembanyama at No. 1 entering the 2026-27 season.

sports.h: Bills beat Rams 37-34 in OT; punch thrown after
sports.b: Buffalo beat the Rams 37-34 in overtime Monday night. Afterward, Rams lineman Alaric Jackson threw an apparent punch at Bills pass-rusher Bradley Chubb.

sports.h: Brewers beat Dodgers 7-4 in NLCS Game 2
sports.b: Milwaukee topped Los Angeles 7-4 in Game 2 of the National League Championship Series.

sports.h: SEC adopts uniform NIL and revenue-share contracts
sports.b: SEC presidents voted Monday to adopt standardized NIL and revenue-share contracts, effective immediately, making the SEC the second power conference to do so after the Big Ten.

sports.h: UCLA QB Iamaleava likely out for season
sports.b: UCLA quarterback Nico Iamaleava is expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury suffered in Saturday's 17-15 win over Oregon, CBS Sports reports.

sports.h: LSU's latest loss puts Kiffin on the spot
sports.b: Lane Kiffin harped on officiating after LSU's second loss in six games, but CBS Sports says questionable late-game decisions start with the coach.

local.h: Hochul, Blakeman spar in governor debate
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican Bruce Blakeman clashed over immigration, Trump and the cost of living in their 60-minute debate Tuesday night.
local.title: NY Gov. Kathy Hochul, Bruce Blakeman spar over immigration, cost of living in debate

local.h: Port Authority bus terminal work starts Thursday
local.b: A decade of disruptions for Midtown Bus Terminal commuters begins Thursday as the Port Authority starts its next construction phase.
local.title: Years of bus headaches start Thursday as Port Authority advances Midtown terminal work

local.h: Dolan hosts Blakeman fundraiser at Knicks game
local.b: Knicks owner James Dolan is hosting a Republican fundraiser for Bruce Blakeman at Thursday's preseason game against the Raptors.
local.title: Dolan's offer: Donations to Blakeman for Knicks tickets

local.h: Officials urge Target boycott over ICE staging
local.b: City officials urged a Target boycott after reports that ICE agents used its Marble Hill store's parking lot as a staging area.
local.title: NYC officials call for Target boycott, say ICE staged at Marble Hill lot before shooting

local.h: Council to vote on carriage horse ban Oct. 22
local.b: Council Speaker Julie Menin said the City Council will vote Oct. 22 on banning Central Park's carriage horse industry.
local.title: NYC Council, Mayor Mamdani agree to end Central Park's carriage horse industry

local.h: 22 NYC food pantries to offer pet food
local.b: Starting Monday, 22 city-funded food pantries will provide dog and cat food using about $500,000 in city funding.
local.title: 22 New York City food pantries to start offering pet food

local.h: NY Public Radio CEO steps down after 8 months
local.b: Christy Tanner, who took over New York Public Radio in February, is stepping down. The organization gave no reason.
local.title: New York Public Radio CEO steps down after 8 months on job

local.h: Cyclist killed by ambulance on Staten Island
local.b: A cyclist riding the wrong way on Richmond Ave in Bulls Head was fatally struck by a turning ambulance Monday night, the NYPD said. The ambulance was not carrying a patient.
local.title: Cyclist dies in wrong-way crash with an ambulance on Staten Island

local.h: Taxi union, Uber seek driver healthcare
local.b: NYC's taxi union has teamed with Uber and a hedge fund to demand healthcare for drivers after four driver deaths.
local.title: NYC's taxi union teams with Uber, private equity firm to demand healthcare after 4 driver deaths

periods.name: Wednesday
periods.text: A slight chance of showers between 11am and 2pm.  Mostly sunny, with a high near 78. West wind 7 to 10 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 20%.

periods.name: Wednesday Night
periods.text: Mostly cloudy, then gradually becoming mostly clear, with a low around 59. North wind 11 to 14 mph.

periods.name: Thursday
periods.text: Sunny, with a steady temperature around 62. North wind 6 to 11 mph.

periods.name: Thursday Night
periods.text: Showers after 2am.  Low around 59. Southeast wind 7 to 11 mph.  Chance of precipitation is 90%. New precipitation amounts of less than a tenth of an inch possible.

periods.name: Friday
periods.text: Showers.  High near 73. Chance of precipitation is 90%. New precipitation amounts between a tenth and quarter of an inch possible.

periods.name: Friday Night
periods.text: Showers, mainly before 8pm.  Low around 48. Breezy.  Chance of precipitation is 80%.
